Your intuition about compositionality is strong; the part I’d correct is that it’s not uniquely a compositional-game-theory idea. What you’re describing first is a compositional causal/mechanical world model. CGT becomes relevant only for the subset of components whose behavior is genuinely strategic.
Don’t ask an agent to carry the world in its prompt. Put the world’s causal structure in reusable components, and let agents operate inside that structure.
The composed world is primary. Agents are just one kind of thing that interacts with it.
The game itself becomes one kind of composable component among other kinds of components. Not the whole world.

Complex worlds should be built compositionally from small, explicit, executable pieces, so that causal dependencies propagate through the structure instead of depending on an agent remembering or inferring the whole system.
CGT contributes one especially valuable family of components: strategic components whose behavior depends on incentives, beliefs, observations and responses of other decision-makers.
